docs.text: Okay, today we’re diving into Lake Michigan! (My personal favorite lake) Lake Michigan’s beaches are covered in a soft, fine sand known as “singing sands” that emit a characteristic squeaking when you walk on them due to their high quartz content
There are many sand beaches along Lake Michigan. If you see stone or concrete adjacent to water, it is reinforcing the shoreline from erosion and isn't meant to be an area for swimming.
The lake michigan beaches are my favorite in the world
As someone who lives near the sandy shores of Lake Michigan, it always surprises me a little when I see the rocky shores.

There is a section of lake Michigan that has a small beach area if you go through the woods over here Its a tidal area so 80% of the time there are too many dead things washing up to make it a good beach Perfect for finding cool stuff washed up from the bay though, lots of sea glass
Sand beaches are one of the coolest things about Lake Michigan.
Oh yeah! Lake Michigan has some fantastic beaches. It’s like swimming in a freshwater ocean. The dunes are pretty neat too.
Michigan summers are gorgeous and Michigan fruit is the best, but Lake Michigan beaches have too many Richie Riches from Chicagoland.

Lake Huron is a good bet for beach. My dad’s family had cottages in a place called Oliphant (haven’t been there for 40 years). Any of that area near Owen Sound is probably good. And lots of places to rent I suspect.

Lake Michigan has beaches, in that they are sandy land formations on a coastline formed by sedimentary deposits via water movement, but that movement is from seiches, not tides. It also lacks salt and real sun, which are key characteristics of the beach. It is *a* beach, but not *the* beach.
Imho, Lake Michigan beaches are undefeated. Give me those singing sands

a lake huron beach ? i live in southern California and a beach to me is an ocean beach...forgetting lakes have beaches too.
